audit_scope.description: Batch 9 focuses on EL components including EVM interpreter internals, trace output generation (EIP-7756), withdrawal processing from CL, P2P transaction announcements (EIP-5793), RPC synchronous transaction submission (EIP-7966), transaction replacement events (EIP-2831), BLAKE2F precompile, MODEXP precompile, EIP versioning (EIP-7577), and fork criteria mechanisms.

in_scope: Validator withdrawal processing from Consensus Layer
MODEXP precompile gas calculation and execution
Fork activation criteria (block number and timestamp based)

misclassified_entities.reason: Transaction Executor is an internal component of the Execution Layer that invokes the VM, not an external entity outside the system boundary. It represents higher-level EL logic calling into the EVM interpreter.
Contract calling BLAKE2F is internal EVM execution context, not external. This represents smart contract code executing within the EVM.
Calling contract for MODEXP is internal smart contract execution within EVM, not an external entity.
Calling contract providing input to MODEXP is internal EVM state, not external.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer (CL) via Engine API - Withdrawals
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Consensus Layer provides validator withdrawal requests via authenticated Engine API. The channel is authenticated with JWT, but withdrawal data (index, validator_index, address, amount) must be validated for field types and ranges. Malicious or buggy CL could send invalid withdrawal data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer (CL) via Engine API - Parent Beacon Root
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL provides parent_beacon_block_root for inclusion in EL block headers. Authenticated channel but EL must validate the beacon root matches actual CL state to prevent RANDAO manipulation attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Nodes via DevP2P - Transaction Announcements
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peers announce transactions via NewPooledTransactionHashes messages. Peers can lie about transaction type and size metadata, requiring validation. DoS mitigation relies on size-based throttling, but malicious peers could send false metadata.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Nodes via DevP2P - Block Propagation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peers transmit block headers and bodies. All block data must be validated against consensus rules including parent hash, state root, transactions root, receipts root, withdrawals root, blob gas fields, and beacon root.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Clients via HTTP/WebSocket - Synchronous TX Submission
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External applications submit transactions via eth_sendRawTransactionSync with optional timeout parameter. Unauthenticated endpoint vulnerable to DoS if timeout limits not enforced. Transaction data must be fully validated. Long-running synchronous connections could exhaust node resources.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Clients via HTTP/WebSocket - Trace Requests
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External tools and debuggers request EVM execution traces via debug_traceTransaction or similar. Unauthenticated access could enable DoS via resource-intensive trace generation. Trace output leaks execution details and should have access controls in production.

trusted_external_entities.name: Users via Wallet Software - Transaction Replacement
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users initiate transaction speed-up, cancellation, or replacement through wallet interfaces. Wallets emit tx_speedup, tx_cancel, tx_replacement events. Malicious wallet could emit false events to DApps. EL must validate replacement invariants (nonce matching, gas increase for speed-up).

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp Event Listeners - Transaction Events
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps listen for transaction replacement events from wallet providers. DApps must not trust events blindly as wallets could be malicious or compromised. This is actually outbound from EL perspective, but DApps are external consumers of EL-originated data via wallet intermediary.

trusted_external_entities.name: EIP Authors via GitHub - Specification Updates
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: GitHub pull requests to ethereum/EIPs repository
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EIP authors submit specification changes via GitHub PRs with version scope indicators (major/minor/patch). Repository tooling validates commit message format, but authors could provide incorrect scope classifications. This affects implementation correctness if developers rely on version numbers for compatibility decisions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producers - Fork Activation Data
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers set block timestamps which can trigger timestamp-based fork activations (post-merge). Validators could manipulate timestamps within consensus bounds to delay or accelerate fork activation. EL must rely on CL consensus for timestamp validity.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Withdrawal index must be valid U64, validator_index must be valid U64, address must be valid 20-byte Address, amount must be valid U256. EL must validate all fields before crediting balance.
Parent beacon block root must match actual CL block hash at specified slot. EL should verify consistency with CL to prevent RANDAO manipulation attacks.
Transaction type and size metadata in announcements may be false. EL must validate actual transaction data upon fetch. Implement per-peer bandwidth throttling based on announced sizes to prevent DoS.

All block header fields must be validated: parent_hash, ommers_hash (must be EMPTY_OMMER_HASH for PoS), state_root, transactions_root, receipt_root, withdrawals_root, blob_gas_used, excess_blob_gas, parent_beacon_block_root. Invalid data must cause block rejection.

Timeout parameter must not exceed node-configured maximum to prevent resource exhaustion. Transaction data must pass all standard validation. Synchronous wait must not block critical node operations. Connection limits must prevent DoS.

Trace generation is computationally expensive. Access should be rate-limited or authenticated. Trace output contains sensitive execution details and should not be exposed publicly in production. Concurrent trace requests could cause memory exhaustion.

Replacement transactions must have matching nonce with pending transaction. For speed-up, recipient, value, and data must match with 10%+ gas increase. For cancel, must be self-send with zero value. Only sender can replace their own transaction (enforced by signature).

Block timestamp determines fork activation for post-merge forks. EL must rely on CL consensus to ensure timestamps are valid and not manipulated. Timestamp-based activation assumes CL prevents timestamp manipulation beyond allowed drift.

coverage_gaps.reason: DApp event listeners are consumers of EL data via wallet providers (outbound data flow), not inbound to EL. No boundary edge required as data flows out from EL.

EIP authors modify specifications in GitHub repository, which is meta-level governance, not runtime data crossing into EL execution. This affects development process but not runtime security boundaries.
